title: Harlem restaurants after the gig
summary: Sheffield Cafe and Wells for breakfast and chicken-and-waffles.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: If you don’t mind my asking just a few other things about Harlem, circa 1950-51? Were there restaurants where musicians liked to eat after the gig?
What were some of those restaurants.

Well, the only place I ate was the Sheffield Café. That was on 126th and 8th Avenue. But most of the musicians used to go up to Wells, and have chicken-and-waffles. Wells Café. That was a famous restaurant.
What sort of food did they have at the Sheffield Café?
Well, they had breakfast food. Bacon, eggs, grits, biscuits.
Yeah. $1.25. That’s all you had to pay.
